source.title: Dataless Model Selection With the Deep Frame Potential

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some equations and figure layouts are flattened, but the results and figure captions are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares architecture families and reports validation error, bearing on V3, but uses its own architecture comparisons rather than the original studies’ methods.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work on random-label fitting and generalization; those cited findings are not this study’s results. Frame-potential values are included only where they are paired with validation-error results relevant to an unlisted claim version.
record.test_reason: The reported comparisons test skip connections, parameter efficiency, and deep frame potential. R1–R6 compare convolutional architectures with one another, not convolutional versus fully connected networks as V3 requires. Fully connected networks appear separately in Figure 4, but the supplied text does not establish a convolutional-versus-fully-connected result. No other claim version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report a correlation between minimum deep frame potential and validation error, and propose it as a data-independent cue for architecture selection and parameter efficiency. They present this as a promising direction rather than an established general guarantee.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes and evaluates a data-independent architecture-selection measure, comparing trained architectures on CIFAR-10 rather than reproducing the original studies’ interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported validation-error relationships vary with architecture family, depth, width, and parameter count.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10, residual connections lower validation error relative to convolutional chain networks, including at matched parameter counts; residual and densely connected architectures scale more efficiently with network size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Skip connections improve validation performance and parameter efficiency relative to the tested convolutional chain architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: Minimum deep frame potential correlates with validation error across the tested architecture families and sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture-dependent minimum deep frame potential predicts validation performance and parameter efficiency in the tested CIFAR-10 networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 4 reports optimization difficulties in some large fully connected networks and improvement after adding deep frame potential regularization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Deep frame potential regularization can improve training and validation performance of some large fully connected networks.

record.problems: Results are presented mainly in figures without numerical values or uncertainty estimates in the text. The paper reports correlation and architecture comparisons, not a causal isolation of local connectivity.

untested.parts: Own experiments comparing random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the same training recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.

A reported convolutional-versus-fully-connected performance comparison; the contribution of local connectivity; learned sparse local connections; convolutional initialization of fully connected networks.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects, including interactions with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, training–test gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures. Deep frame potential measures a different construct.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the extracted V3 limits_scope verdict: failing to isolate local connectivity is an untested component, not evidence limiting V3. Numerical point values cannot be recovered reliably from the flattened figures, but the textual descriptions support the separate skip-connection findings.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Whether test error keeps falling beyond the width needed for zero training error; no interpolation-threshold analysis is reported.

The comparisons are on CIFAR-10; the paper does not isolate local connectivity from other architectural differences, test learned sparse connections in fully connected networks, or test convolutional initialization of a fully connected network.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers and their held-out performance.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptation of training recipes.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbation sharpness and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures; the paper measures deep frame potential instead.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

relation.reason: The paper discusses overparameterization, random-label memorization, and generalization as motivation, but its own results address different architectural and representation properties.

tranche.reason: The experiments evaluate architecture selection, frame potential, and skip connections. R1–R6 compare convolutional architectures; Figure 4 separately studies fully connected networks without establishing the V3 comparison. No interpolation threshold is established for V2, and no other claim version is tested or used as a tool.

source_check.notes: Exact validation-error values and uncertainty estimates are not stated in the prose; retaining figure-only values is appropriate. The authors’ conclusion is accurately paraphrased as a correlation and promising architecture-selection direction.
